LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 3.1.1 LISTENING COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.1: Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension, part of Strand 3 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What should one look for when listening to a text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the main idea from a cause and effect text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. pinpoint specific information from a cause and effect text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. infer the meanings of unfamiliar words using context clues,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the importance of listening for detail.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify the main idea from a cause and effect text,

   Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. pinpoint specific information from a cause and effect text,

   Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. infer the meanings of unfamiliar words using context clues,

   Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. acknowledge the importance of listening for detail.

   Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to a cause and effect text on pollution being read by the teacher or from a digital device,

2. pick out the main idea from that cause and effect text,

3. respond to oral questions based on the text correctly,

4. identify and write down the ideas presented in the text,

5. orally answer questions based on the text,

6. make a list of unfamiliar words and practise pronouncing them,

7. give the meaning of specific words using context clues,

8. look up the meanings of unfamiliar words from an online or offline dictionary,

9. use given words to construct sentences.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to a cause and effect text on pollution being read by the teacher or from a digital device,
2. pick out the main idea from that cause and effect text,
3. respond to oral questions based on the text correctly,
4. identify and write down the ideas presented in the text,
5. orally answer questions based on the text,
6. make a list of unfamiliar words and practise pronouncing them,
7. give the meaning of specific words using context clues,
8. look up the meanings of unfamiliar words from an online or offline dictionary,
9. use given words to construct sentences.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: It is enhanced as learner listens to texts and searches for meanings of words using digital devices.

• Self- efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner practices pronouncing words and uses them correctly in sentences.

Values:
Responsibility: It is cultivated as the learner acquires knowledge about how to take care of the environment from the cause and

effect text on pollution.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental education awareness: It is enhanced as the learner listens to a text on pollution.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner relates good listening skills to the learning of listening in Kiswahili.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify the main idea from a cause and effect text,
2. pinpoint specific information from a cause and effect text,
3. infer the meanings of unfamiliar words using context clues,
4. acknowledge the importance of listening for detail.

Remember the key question: What should one look for when listening to a text?
